column2: STYLE: 1980s teletext (Ceefax). Everything is built from 2x3 mosaic block graphics in character cells (about 4x5 px cells, so each mosaic pixel is ~2 px), eight pure teletext colours on black, a page header with page number, flashing and double-height attributes. THEME: the weather map page. Each numeral is a mosaic-block weather front or cloud over a blocky map of the British Isles, raining blue blocks, sun symbols pulsing, wind arrows stepping on every beat. Minute turn: the page reloads row by row (as real teletext does) with the new front. Hour: page 302 cycles to the next sub-page, the time still reading.

STYLE: Javanese wayang kulit shadow puppetry. Intricately perforated leather puppets seen as silhouettes on a warm cotton screen lit by a flickering oil lamp, with the painted-colour side glimpsed when a puppet nears the screen, buffalo-horn control rods visible, the gunungan (tree-of-life puppet). THEME: each numeral is a puppet, its long arms on rods posed into the digit's shape; on every beat of the gamelan the puppeteer flicks the arms and they quiver. Minute turn: the old puppet sweeps off and the new one enters. Hour: the gunungan crosses the screen to change the scene, the time still reading.

STYLE: Seurat's pointillism (Le Chahut). The whole image is small dots of pure unmixed colour (complementaries placed side by side so they mix in the eye), dots about 2 px, no lines. THEME: a Paris café-concert can-can. Each numeral is a dancer, kicking legs and frilled skirts held in the digit's shape, kicking on every beat of the band, the gaslight sparkling. Minute turn: the dancer high-kicks off and the next one cartwheels in. Hour: the whole chorus line's finale, the time still reading.

STYLE: Mondrian's Broadway Boogie Woogie. A grid of yellow lines on off-white, the lines broken into small squares of red, blue and grey that move along them like traffic and music, larger flat colour blocks, nothing else. THEME: the city at night: each numeral is a city block of the grid, its edges lined with pulsing traffic squares that hop along on every beat, syncopated like boogie-woogie piano. Minute turn: the traffic re-routes and the grid reorganises into the new digit. Hour: rush hour, everything flows, the time still reading.

STYLE: Persian miniature painting. Flat jewel colours (lapis, malachite, vermilion, gold leaf), a high horizon and no perspective, tiled patterns, fine dark outlines, gold sky, tiny rocks and flowering trees. THEME: a royal polo match. Each numeral is a horse and rider in full gallop, the horse's neck and legs and the rider's mallet arm bent into the digit's shape, galloping on every beat (legs cycling, tails flying), the ball skidding between them. Minute turn: the rider rides off and the new one gallops in. Hour: the goal and the king's celebration, the time still reading.

STYLE: Egyptian tomb painting. Flat ochre, red, black, blue and green on limestone plaster, register lines, figures in strict profile, columns of hieroglyphs, a little flaking. THEME: each numeral is built of hieroglyph signs and profile figures (a heron, a reed, a coiled rope, a striding scribe) that act on every beat: the heron dips, the scribe writes, the reed sways. Minute turn: a painter re-paints the register with the new digit, outline then fill. Hour: Ra's solar boat sails across the top register, the time still reading.

STYLE: spirograph drawn with gel pens on black paper. Hypotrochoid and epitrochoid curves in metallic and glitter ink, pens skipping slightly, the plastic gear wheels visible as translucent rings with pin holes. THEME: each numeral is drawn by a spirograph wheel rolling along a track shaped like the digit, laying a looping garland that forms the digit; the wheels keep rolling, overdrawing the loops so they shimmer, and the pen colour shifts on every beat. Minute turn: the paper slides and a new track is pinned for the new digit. Hour: a giant rosette, the time still reading.

STYLE: 1940s film noir. Black and white only with deep blacks, film grain, venetian-blind light stripes slanting across everything, rain on the window, a neon sign blinking outside. THEME: a detective's office. Each numeral is cigarette smoke curling into the digit's shape, rising and swirling, puffed out fresh on every beat by an unseen smoker, stripes of light cutting through it. Minute turn: a draught blows the old smoke away and a fresh puff curls into the new digit. Hour: the blinds snap open, a lightning flash, the time still reading.

STYLE: latte art seen from above. Microfoam white on espresso brown (crema tones, flat), the cup rim and saucer, pour lines and the etching-tool marks of a barista, a little sheen. THEME: each numeral is poured as latte art (a rosetta stroke bent into the digit, hearts as bowls), the foam drifting and the pattern wobbling as the cup is tapped on every beat. Minute turn: the cup is swirled and the old digit stretches into a spiral and dissolves while a fresh pour lays the new one. Hour: a full swan pour, the time still reading.

STYLE: South Indian kolam: white rice-flour lines drawn freehand around a grid of dots (pulli) on a damp dark doorstep, plus a few rangoli powder colours, slightly grainy and uneven. THEME: each numeral is one continuous kolam line looping around its dots, drawn by a hand that keeps tracing it; on every beat the flour line brightens and ripples as it is re-sprinkled, and ants march along it. Minute turn: the morning sweep brushes the old one away and a new kolam is drawn around new dots. Hour: a festival rangoli in colour, the time still reading.

STYLE: Swiss topographic map. Contour lines in brown, blue lakes with depth lines, black rock hachures, red trails, fine map lettering, flat paper colour (no hillshading). THEME: each numeral is a mountain ridge whose summit contours trace the digit; the contours breathe on every beat and hikers (red dots) march up the trails while clouds drift over. Minute turn: tectonic time-lapse: the old ridge erodes contour by contour while the new one rises. Hour: an avalanche or alpenglow, the time still reading.

STYLE: letterpress printing with wood type. Flat ink with the slightly uneven coverage and halo of a press impression, deep bite into soft cream paper, overprinted colours, wood grain in large solids, worn edges. THEME: a print shop: the numerals ARE wood type blocks locked in the press bed; on every beat the platen presses, ink rollers sweep over them and the fresh impression shows. Minute turn: the compositor pulls the old block and drops the new one in. Hour: a multi-colour poster run, the time still reading.

STYLE: Van Gogh's impasto brushwork. The whole image is thick short brushstrokes of flat colour following a flow field (each stroke a little dash, flat, no lighting), cobalt and ultramarine sky, lemon yellow stars with halo rings, a flame-like cypress. THEME: each numeral is a swirl of wind in the starry sky, its strokes streaming along the digit's shape; the swirls pulse and the stars' halos throb on every beat. Minute turn: the wind blows the old swirl apart and the new one curls in. Hour: a comet, the time still reading.

STYLE: Keith Haring. Thick black outlines, flat bright fills (red, yellow, green, blue), little motion marks and radiating lines, figures without faces, all-over composition on a bright ground. THEME: each numeral is a dancing Haring figure (or a stack of them) bent into the digit's shape; on every beat they jump, the motion marks flash, a barking dog and a radiant baby join in. Minute turn: the old figure jumps off and the new one breakdances into the next digit. Hour: everyone dances in a chain, the time still reading.

STYLE: a worn VHS tape. Chroma bleed and colour offset, scanlines, tracking noise bands rolling up, an on-screen "PLAY" overlay, slightly washed-out 1980s colours, tape wobble. THEME: an 1980s aerobics workout video. Each numeral is an aerobics instructor in leotard and leg warmers, their pose forming the digit, doing a move on every beat (step, kick, arm raise) while the class follows behind. Minute turn: a tracking glitch tears across and the next instructor is in the new pose. Hour: the cool-down routine with the whole class, the time still reading.

STYLE: kintsugi. A broken celadon or raku bowl seen from above, flat glaze colour with a little crackle and one soft sheen, the breaks repaired with lines of gold lacquer. THEME: the gold seams ARE the numerals; molten gold flows along them, pulsing on every beat, glints travelling along the lines. Minute turn: the bowl cracks along the new digit's lines and gold is poured into them while the old seams fade into the glaze. Hour: the bowl is shattered and rebuilt, the time still reading.
